segments.text: Chapter eight. The helping kasra, from Stage 2.
A word cannot end in sukūn right before al.
So the sukūn becomes a small kasra. The verb is still fixed.
Open the door.
اِفْتَحِ البَابَ
The order verb ends in sukūn. Before al, it takes a small kasra.
It is still built on sukūn.
The girl did not write the lesson.
مَا كَتَبَتِ البِنْتُ الدَّرْسَ
Here the kasra sits on the ḥarf at the end of the verb.
And the word for not changes nothing.
This kasra is only a bridge for speaking. It is not jarr, and not iʿrāb.
In short.
Past and order verbs are fixed. The present verb is mostly flexible. It comes in Stage 8.
The past verb has fourteen persons.
Endings like these are doer pronouns, in the place of rafʿ. But the ending of she wrote is a ḥarf.
The past verb is built on fatha, on damma, or on sukūn.
To say did not, put this word before a past verb.
مَا كَتَبَ
It is a ḥarf with no place.
The order verb is built on sukūn, or on dropping the noon.
A middle damma gives alif with damma. Otherwise, alif with kasra.
Now it is your turn. Open the Practice tab.
Choose the past form, say what it is built on, and give the order.
Good luck.
